evidence_items.locator: Quarterly Trends, Operating Expenses, Compute and Infrastructure (p. 158–159)

receipt.public_excerpt:
Compute and infrastructure expenses increased sequentially in each of the quarters presented, from $944
million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 to $5.6 billion for the three months ended June 30, 2026

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic's compute spending rose every quarter of 2025 within his window. The S-1 table shows $944M, $1,390M and $2,047M for Q1–Q3 2025. There was no quarter of reduction.

evidence_items.locator: MD&A, Operating Expenses, Compute and Infrastructure (p. 151)

receipt.public_excerpt:
Compute and infrastructure expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $4.8 billion, or 190%,
compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: Compute spending nearly tripled from 2024 ($2,522M) to 2025 ($7,326M). This is consistent with costs rising across his window. The 2025 total includes Q4 2025, which falls outside it.

receipt.public_excerpt:
Net cash used in operating activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 decreased by $3.1 billion compared
to the year ended December 31, 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: Operating cash burn fell from $5,692M (2024) to $2,637M (2025), and H1 2025 was $1,513M. If 'burns' means cash burn, this cuts against him. The filing attributes the fall to using up prepaid hosting and to payment timing, alongside rising cloud costs, not to cost-cutting.

metric_scope.metric: Net cash used in operating activities

unresolved_gaps: Anthropic's AWS-specific monthly bills, the data he relied on, are not public.
The S-1 gives quarterly figures only from Q1 2025. For 2024 I found only an annual total, so a dip within 2024 cannot be ruled out.
